entries.title: Ruth 1:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 Elimelech, driven by famine into Moab, dies there. 4 Mahlon and Chilion, having married wives of Moab, die also. 6 Naomi, returning homeward, 8 dissuades her two daughters-in-law from going with her. 14 Orpah leaves her, but Ruth with great constancy accompanies her. 19 They two come to Beth-lehem, where they are gladly received.

entries.title: Ruth 1:11
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
are there.This alludes to the custom that when a married brother died, without leaving posterity, his brother should take his widow; and the children of such marriages were accounted those of the deceased brother. This address of Naomi to her daughter-in-law is exceedingly tender, persuasive, and affecting.

entries.title: Ruth 1:14
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
Orpah. Ge 31:28,55; 1Ki 19:20; Mt 10:37; 19:22; Mr 10:21,22; 2Ti 4:10 but Ruth.The LXX. add, [kai epestrepsen eis ton laon autes,] "and returned to her own people." The Vulgate, Syriac, and Arabic are to the same purpose. It seems a very natural addition, and agrees with the assertion in the next verse; and is accordingly adopted by Houbigant as a part of the text.
